newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade up 7.1 pct yr/yr in Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade up 7.1 pct yr/yr in Jan-May.

text.p: Taiwan's trade with rival China grew 7.1 percent to US$9.239 billion in the first five months of 1997, compared to the same 1996 period, the Board of Foreign Trade said on Monday.
The bilateral trade figure represented 9.8 percent of Taiwan's total foreign trade, a board statement said.
Taiwan's exports to the communist mainland rose an annual 4.8 percent in January-May to $7.764 billion, while Taiwan's imports from China jumped 21.2 percent to $1.475 billion, the statement said.
The significant import growth was mainly due to a steady economic recovery in Taiwan, fuelling demand for China's raw materials and semi-finished products.
In January-May, Taiwan enjoyed a trade surplus of $6.289 billion, up 1.5 percent year-on-year, it said.
In May alone, two-way trade was up 11.3 percent to $2.03 billion from May 1996, it said.

China has considered Taiwan a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949. Taiwan bans direct contact with China. All trade with China must be conducted through a third region, mostly Hong Kong.
Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested more than $30 billion in China since an unofficial thaw began in the late 1980s. Trade has grown despite a new political freeze dating to mid-1995.
